doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
title: Eddie South trio in California with Lionel Hampton nearby
summary: Hinton's first trip to California, a trio with Everett Boxdale and Eddie South at the Club Ballyhoo, Lionel Hampton welcoming them, and Carmen Miranda on the bill.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. From there we went to California, my first trip to California. Now Lionel Hampton and I had gone to school together and Lionel had married Gladys and moved to California.

Yeah, he was married then. In 1933 he was married to Gladys. And Gladys… they moved to California because Gladys was an excellent seamstress and she got a job sewing for one of the great movie stars, Gloria Swanson or one of the big move stars. She had a good job. Lionel got the job out there working with Les Hiss band. We grew up together so he was….Lionel met us at the railroad station, the little group playing for us as we came into town.

We got a job at the… at least I got a job in a club on Sunset Boulevard called the Club Ballyhoo, another small club. All of the violin players in the movie theater… orchestra, they‟d heard about Eddie . We‟ve only got three pieces now. This is a trio. Everett Boxdale, Eddie South, and myself.

Yeah. We were really cooking. We had [unintelligible] a few of those things that Eddie taught us, Rhapsody In Blue, American In Paris, After The Ball, and [Unintelligible], The Sentiment’s Not Yours, Hungarian songs. We got to play in this small club and it was where all these little players from the movies came out to hear. That‟s the first time I really saw guys writing on their cuff. The guys would be writing on their cuff. We played there. There was dance team, a trio, a dance team that danced in parts of the show. A trio, a girl and two boys. The girl Carman Miranda and one of the boy dancers was Caesar Romero. I don‟t know who the other guy was. That was 1933. A very successful… Buck Clayton was on his way to China. He had come out [unintelligible] I remember distinctly.
We had a very successful engagement and came back to Chicago and things just went on from there.
